d2.text:
Device plan, 25 Nov 2026.

For labs that already have their own system. We give the device with alerts, by device QR and passport QR binding.

1. Scan the device QR, pick the temperature type.
2. Scan each passport QR: bound. If it will not scan, type the code.
3. Time limit counts from the first tube.
4. One device, one temperature type.
5. Breach: the alert and the report say how far and how long. The lab decides in its own system whether to receive the sample.
6. Scanning a passport onto the next device releases it from the last. Empty the device when the samples are handed over.
7. Lab system link: optional, switched on by Track0tic if the lab wants its data sent.

Not in this plan: work orders, gate pass, receiving bench, nonconformities, site and agency masters, walk-in and lab to lab flows. Lid opening alert is under development.

n1.text:
Track0tic Lab: generic demo lab, first cut 24 Nov 2026. Apollo portal structure with the lab capability map inside.

Evidence, not a LIMS: no patient name, no test, no result. The passport QR number is the only key.

Two ways to collect: at the patient's home (Pro box, trip to the lab), or the patient walks in to the lab or a centre (tube straight into the fridge, no box). The phlebotomist is marked Own staff or Other: same login, same steps.

1. Home: collector logs in (mobile + code), scans the Pro box, then pastes and scans a label on every tube. Booking number only.
2. Seal: the trip starts. After that every lid opening is recorded.
3. Collection centre: tubes are bound to the centre fridge (HUB), then moved to a Pro box for the run to the lab.
4. Lab bench: every tube is scanned to check the count, then Accept / Accept with deviation / Reject. A box that went out of range cannot be accepted without a reason and a note.
5. Accepted tubes are bound to a lab fridge (HUB) or released to testing.
6. Anyone scans the tube: report, no login. Staff who log in see the fuller Quality Handling Report.
7. Lab to another lab for the next test: same label, one more leg. Own lab: Pro box with our staff, decided at that lab's bench. Outside lab: Lite box by courier, received from a link.

n2.text:
Decided by Claude for this cut. Change any of them.

Collectors log in with mobile number and code, as in Apollo. This replaces the earlier idea of device QR alone or QR + PIN.

Bench decision is per box, and one tube can be rejected alone.

Lite has no lid sensor: Seal is a button.

Tube type is picked from a list set by the lab. One box carries one temperature profile.

Decision overdue after 2 hours. Alert after 5 minutes outside the range. Both are settings.

Referral lab is in, on the Lite, with a no-login link to mark it received.

Site IDs (L001, CC101, RL201) and device names (HUB-L001A, PRO-L001-04) are samples, following the Apollo naming rule.

Public report shows only Storage and Transit steps: no site, no collector, no inside remark.

Same as Apollo and Axis for symmetry: work orders with gate pass, device cards with colour, GRN, label orders, masters with Excel upload, optional KYC, Excel/CSV/PDF reports, audit log for the admin only.

New for the lab: Receiving Bench, Storage Units with daily record, Nonconformities, Calibration, Temperature Profiles.

n3.text:
What closes each loop.

Device: sent by Track0tic, GRN, fitted to a site, in use, sent back.
Box: scanned to start, sealed, arrived, decided, free again.
Tube: bound to a box, bench scan, decision, lab fridge, scanned out to testing.
Missing tube: Not received, nonconformity opened.
Rejected tube: reason recorded, shown on its report.
Lite: marked received from the link, alert from day 2 if not back.
Alert: back in range, or closed with a remark.
Nonconformity: closed with the action taken.
Anything stuck: closed by the Lab Admin with a remark.
